$comment: THE DECLARATION. One row per structured identifier racecar recognises: how to find it,
how to confirm it, whose rule it is, and where that rule is published.
This file is the single home. scripts/identifiers.py implements the algorithms named here
and nothing else; check_content_blind.py consumes the result. Adding a type is a row, not
a code change, unless it needs an algorithm nobody has implemented yet.
EVERY ROW CITES ITS ISSUING AUTHORITY, and is written from that document. A type nobody
can source that way does not go in.
SHAPE IS NOT ENOUGH, WHICH IS WHAT `check` IS FOR. Every regex here matches far more than
it should; the algorithm is what turns a match into evidence. A row whose check is `none`
is claiming its shape alone is rare enough in prose, which is the weakest claim available
and is always stated in `evidence`.
`evidence` SAYS WHY THE RULE DISCRIMINATES, and nothing else -- not what a reader might
get wrong, not what an earlier version did. A measured acceptance rate on arbitrary
strings of the same shape is the strongest form it takes; a closed enumeration with
positional meaning is the next. It carries no `$` because a gate holds rows to it.
EVERY ROW RECORDS THE TWO RATES ITS TIER RESTS ON. `shape_acceptance_pct` is how much of
arbitrary strings OF THE ROW'S OWN SHAPE the check accepts -- the structure given away, so
the arithmetic is isolated. `ambient_claim_pct` is how much of arbitrary tokens of the same
LENGTH, over the repertoire the row's characters live in, the row claims outright: shape and
check together, against the population a scanner meets. For a bare row the two coincide,
because its shape is the whole repertoire and there is nothing for the ambient draw to fail.
`anchored` IS A CLAIM ABOUT THOSE NUMBERS. scripts/tests/test_identifiers.py re-derives both
on every run and refuses a table where an anchored row claims arbitrary tokens as freely as
the best-discriminating row on the opt-in side -- a row that does is running in every
governed repo on the evidence the opt-in exists to gate. Re-measuring is what keeps them
true: a rate nobody re-derives drifts, and these did.
BOUNDARIES ARE DECLARED, NOT BAKED IN. `left` and `right` name a boundary rule rather
than embedding a lookbehind, because Go's RE2 and POSIX ERE have no lookaround at all.
KEYS BEGINNING WITH `$` ARE DOCUMENTATION. JSON has no comment syntax, so this borrows
JSON Schema's convention: ignore any key starting with `$`.
NAMES FOLLOW THE REGION, because the region is already a field. `<cc>-<type>` with `cc`
the row's ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 lowercased; a genuinely global type carries no prefix, which
is the same null the `country` field uses. This is Google Cloud DLP's infoType convention
(US_SOCIAL_SECURITY_NUMBER, INDIA_AADHAAR_INDIVIDUAL) and python-stdnum's module path
(stdnum.<cc>.<type>) rather than anything invented here.
It is not cosmetic. `pan` meant India's Permanent Account Number in a table that also
holds payment cards, where PAN is the Primary Account Number -- two different things
under one name, in one file.

boundaries.word: a word boundary (\b in most dialects)
boundaries.not-digit: the adjacent character must not be a digit
boundaries.not-digit-or-dot: the adjacent character must not be a digit or a period

$comment: How to FIND a candidate, never how to judge one. Runs of three or more digits joined by
single spaces or hyphens, in any arrangement, so no grouping convention is privileged.
A fully permissive variant -- a separator between any two digits -- examines 21 candidates
in racecar's own tree where this examines 9, and claims exactly the same 3. The checksum
does all of the filtering, so the extra permissiveness buys nothing but scan cost.

algorithms.luhn: Luhn mod 10 over the digits, check digit included (ISO/IEC 7812-1)
algorithms.luhn-prefixed: Luhn over params.prefix concatenated with the value
algorithms.luhn-alnum: Luhn over the value with letters expanded to two digits (A=10..Z=35)
algorithms.iso7064-mod97: ISO 7064 mod-97-10 over the alphanumeric-expanded value, == 1
algorithms.iso7064-mod97-iban: as above, after moving the first four characters to the end
algorithms.verhoeff: the Verhoeff dihedral check over the digits
algorithms.mod11-two-digit: two trailing mod-11 check digits over params.weights
algorithms.none: no arithmetic; the shape, an enumeration, or `context` carries the evidence
algorithms.schema: the named scheme decides validity outright: positional meaning over closed enumerations, no arithmetic

$comment: PAYMENT CARDS. A 15-digit number is either an Amex or it is not, once you have all
fifteen digits. The IIN, the exact length and Luhn decide it; nothing else is consulted.
IIN AND LENGTH ARE CHECKED JOINTLY. Checked apart, a 15-digit number beginning 4 reads
as a Visa, and no Visa is 15 digits.
GROUPING IS NOT EVIDENCE AND IS NOT RECORDED HERE. How a human spaced the digits is
presentation. Enumerating each brand's convention would only move the hole -- a
hyphenated Amex, or one spaced unconventionally, would still be lost -- so separators
are stripped before anything is judged. See `payment_card_scan`.
MEASURED. Arbitrary digit runs claimed as some brand: 0.170% at 15 digits, 0.320% at
14, 2.190% at 16 -- stronger than ABA at 3.84% or Aadhaar at 9.97%, both of which this
table already trusts on arithmetic alone.

$comment: SAID OUT LOUD. A perimeter is defined by both edges, and a type considered and refused is
more useful recorded than silently absent: the next reader would otherwise re-derive the
same answer, or add the row.
Two grounds, and they are not the same. NOT A DETECTOR: the rule accepts too large a share
of arbitrary strings of its own shape, and the `reason` gives the measured rate. OUT OF
SCOPE: the type would work, but it is outside the jurisdictions or classes this table
covers.

types.name: duns
types.reason: Nine digits, no check digit (the mod-10 one was discontinued), no structure. Accepts 100% of nine-digit runs.

types.name: us-ssn-bare
types.reason: The issuance exclusions alone accept 88.81% of arbitrary nine-digit runs, measured. The dash is what makes SSN detectable.

types.name: us-ein-bare
types.reason: The campus prefix set alone accepts 82.99%, measured. Same conclusion as SSN.

types.name: in-micr
types.reason: RBI publishes MICR as nine digits -- city, bank, branch -- with no check digit, so it accepts 100% of nine-digit runs and is indistinguishable from any nine-digit token.

types.name: gb-utr
types.reason: HMRC publishes the ten-digit format but NOT a check digit algorithm. A widely-circulated weighted mod-11 exists in third-party code; it fails this table's provenance bar, and without it the row accepts 100% of ten-digit runs.

types.name: gb-sortcode
types.reason: Six digits with no checksum: 100% of six-digit runs. The Vocalink modulus check validates a sort code WITH an account number against a weights table that is periodically reissued, and shipping a copy would mis-validate silently as it goes stale.

types.name: eu-vat
types.reason: Twenty-seven member-state formats with twenty-seven separate check rules. Out of scope: the perimeter is four jurisdictions, not every country's codes.

types.name: gb-upn
types.reason: English Unique Pupil Number. Genuinely PII, but education-sector; no governed repo touches it.

types.name: bic
types.reason: ISO 9362 defines no check digit, so the only evidence is the shape -- eight uppercase alphanumerics whose 5th and 6th characters form an ISO 3166 country code. Measured, that claims 37.6% of arbitrary eight-letter uppercase tokens, and in racecar's own tree it read MESSAGES, MARKDOWN, VERBATIM and PROVIDER as BICs. Prose is full of ALLCAPS words; this is a rule against writing them.

$comment: PARAMETERS, not logic. An algorithm above is a pure function; a scheme is the data it
is applied WITH. Keeping them apart is what lets a new jurisdiction be a row plus a
scheme rather than a patch to the code.
Every scheme here is the published rule of the authority the row cites. Where a list is
an enumeration that changes over time (RTO codes, ISO country codes) it is data for the
same reason: it will change, and it should change here rather than in a function.

us-ssn.$note: `void` are numbers the SSA issued and then withdrew after they appeared on specimen cards and in advertising -- 078-05-1120 was in a 1938 Woolworth wallet and was used by tens of thousands of people. They identify nobody, so reporting one is a false positive.

us-itin.$note: Group 93 is reserved out of these ranges for ATIN.

in-cin.$note: Field offsets are data because the layout is the rule: 1 listing status, 5 industry, 2 state, 4 year, 3 ownership type, 6 registration number.

$comment: RTO code -> current ISO 3166-2 subdivision. NOT an identity mapping, and that is the
whole point of holding it as data. ISO aligned four codes to the vehicle codes on
2023-11-23 (OR->OD, CT->CG, TG->TS, UT->UK), so those now agree. What does not agree
is history: DD (Daman and Diu) and DN (Dadra and Nagar Haveli) remain on licences
issued before the 2020 merger, and ISO now lists only IN-DH.
